findings.reason: a graph-write node that cannot show its authority refuses anything passes on a validator that was silently disabled, and every sibling write node in this plan carries that arm (§20 "the test fails when the edge write is removed"; §7–§18 "fails with the fix reverted"), so this is a missing control, not a preference.
findings.text: §31 (and, identically, §32 at :225 and §33 at :229) declares "183 admitted and 0 refused" as its outcome, and neither section drives a row the signed authority should refuse, so a preview whose validation never runs reads the same as a clean one

findings.reason: §31 tells each node to re-read the split from a census that recommends reclassification while §31's ruling records a retirement, so without an explicit "overrides §30's remedy" statement a node meets two contradictory instructions and can reclassify (or block) instead of record.
findings.text: §31 asserts the 183 have no producing source and "are correct orphan retirements that lack their record", but the census it cites (`sib-superseded-lineage-census.html`, the §30 fragment) classes exactly these 208 names (`maintenance_only_change_log` 96 + `no_change_recorded` 112) with the opposite remedy, "a reclassification out of superseded — no supersession event exists to justify the stage", and the source-less orphan retirements the census does record (`supersede_exhausted_orphan`, 281 names) are a different class §31 does not touch
